verdict.rationale: GitBook documents a dedicated 'GitBook Agent' that reviews change requests, an AI Assistant that flags and fixes outdated content, and a live write-capable MCP server that can open change requests programmatically — covering drafting/updating/reviewing docs and shipping via change requests. However, evidence for prompt-, PR-, and schedule-triggered workflows specifically is thin (mostly implied via Git sync and 'flags then fixes' claims) and all evidence is vendor-authored docs with no independent/hands-on confirmation of the agent's autonomous behavior. Missing for 10: independent corroboration of the agent's autonomous drafting/scheduling behavior, explicit documentation of schedule-based triggers, and third-party validation that agent-authored change requests work end-to-end.
